description: Look up a verified tax or accounting rule by its key. The system automatically routes to the active company's own country library: every live country has one (e.g. India: gst-rate-slabs, personal-income-tax-slabs-new-regime), so never tell a user you only know UK rules. Use this for ANY question about specific deadlines, thresholds, notice periods, regulatory dates, or rules where being wrong would mislead the user. UK examples: vat-registration-threshold, ct-filing-deadline, mtd-itsa-mandatory-50k, dividend-allowance-2026-27, mileage-rates-2026-27. UAE examples: ct-rates, ct-filing-deadline, vat-rate, free-zone-qfzp, no-personal-income-tax. Returns the exact answer + an official source URL you MUST cite in your reply, and where the rule has a validity period, the dates it applies between. ALWAYS prefer this over stating a rule from memory. Apply the rule to the user's facts: when the answer turns on a fact only the user knows (when goods were delivered, when work was finished, when money arrived), ask for that fact, never for the conclusion (ask "when did you deliver it?", not "does it belong in Q3 or October?"). Once the user gives the fact, that is the fact: state the result the rule gives for it, with the source, and do not add that you cannot check it or that their accountant should confirm it. Point to an accountant only when the rule itself leaves the question open. For a question about a PAST period, or a FUTURE one (next year's rates where a budget has already set them), pass as_of so you get the rule for that date rather than the current one. If you do not know the exact key, call list_tax_rules first.

as_of.description: Optional ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the answer must be true for. Pass this whenever the question is about a PAST period - a prior-year return, an old invoice, a historic filing - or a FUTURE one such as next year's rates, because rates change and the current rule may not be the one that applies then. The system walks the rule history and returns the version in force on that date, plus the period it applies to. Omit for questions about today: the answer is then the version in force today. A next-year rule may not be law yet; its answer says so.

company.description: Which company to read, by name or id, when the account has more than one (see list_companies). Leave it out to use the only company, or the default.

country.description: ISO country code of the business, such as GB, IE or US. Pass it when the user has not connected AccountsOS. Once connected, leave it out and their company's country is used.

key.description: The rule key. Use list_tax_rules to see all available keys for the active company's country.
